mainTopic: Koshering a vessel's rim (כבולעו כך פולטו), making a non-Jew's knife usable by שפה and נעיצה, the story of שבור מלכא, and the end of מסכת עבודה זרה
overview: The גמרא first finishes a story about koshering the rim of a vessel. A ring of dough was built around the rim, and the vessel was filled with water and boiled, so drops of boiling water reached the rim. רבא praises רב עקביא for this idea and explains it with the rule כבולעו כך פולטו: the rim took in the forbidden taste through small drops, so small drops can release it. Then the גמרא turns to the משנה's rule that polishing a knife (שפה) makes it usable. The אמוראים add details: stick it into the ground ten times, use hard untilled earth, and use only a smooth knife with no notches. A ברייתא backs this up, and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע says this method works only for eating cold food. A story shows the method in action: שבור מלכא thrust his knife into the ground ten times before cutting an אתרוג for מר יהודה, but not for באטי בר טובי, whom he did not trust to be careful. The amud closes with the הדרן for פרק השוכר את הפועל, which ends מסכת עבודה זרה.

steps.title: A dough rim lets the boiling water reach the vessel's lip
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes describing how a vessel was koshered: a ring of dough was placed around its rim, then it was filled with water and boiled.
steps.simpleTranslation: He made a ring of dough around its rim, filled it with water, and boiled it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a description, begun before this point, of how someone koshered a vessel all the way up to its rim. The dough wall let the boiling water bubble up and splash onto the rim.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rim is the hard spot, because water in an ordinary pot cannot cover the very top edge. Raising the edge with dough lets drops of the boiling water reach the lip, and the next step explains why that is enough.

phrases.english: a rim of dough around its mouth,
and filled it with water and boiled it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the description of the koshering method from the text before this point.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vessel's rim can be koshered by building it up with dough and boiling water to the top.

steps.title: רבא praises רב עקביא and explains why the method works
steps.stepSummary: רבא says only a great person like רב עקביא would think of this. He explains it with the rule כבולעו כך פולטו: the rim took in the forbidden taste through little drops, so it can release it through little drops of boiling water.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Who would be clever enough to do such a thing, if not רב עקביא, who is a great man? He holds that the way a vessel absorbs is the way it releases. Just as the rim absorbed through small drops, it also releases through small drops.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא praises the method and gives the reason behind it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think the rim needs to sit fully in boiling water. רבא explains that the rim never sat in the forbidden food. It only took in splashes. So splashes of boiling water are enough to draw the taste back out, which is the rule כבולעו כך פולטו.

keyTerms.meaning: As it absorbs, so it releases: koshering matches how the taste went in

steps.whatToRemember: כבולעו כך פולטו: a vessel is koshered the same way it took in the forbidden taste. If it absorbed through splashes, splashes can release it.
steps.whyThisMatters: כבולעו כך פולטו is a basic rule of הכשר כלים that shows up all through הלכה.

phrases.english: Rava said: Who is clever enough
to do such a thing,
if not Rav Akavya,
since he is a great man?
He holds: as it absorbs, so it expels.
Just as it absorbs through small drops,
so too it expels through small drops.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מַאן חַכִּים לְמֶעְבַּד כִּי הָא מִילְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the method just described.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Since the rim absorbed through splashes, splashes of boiling water are enough to kosher it.

steps.title: The משנה: polishing a knife makes it usable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: a knife bought from a non-Jew is polished, and then it is usable.
steps.simpleTranslation: The knife: one polishes it, and it is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה about koshering a knife. It is setting up the explanations the אמוראים will add next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'pure' means the knife is permitted for use. Polishing scrapes off whatever forbidden material is stuck to the surface of the blade.

phrases.english: The knife: one polishes it and it is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A knife becomes usable by polishing it.

steps.title: Sticking the knife into the ground ten times
steps.stepSummary: רב עוקבא בר חמא says that along with polishing, one also sticks the knife into the ground ten times.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עוקבא בר חמא said: And one sticks it into the ground ten times.
steps.whatsHappening: רב עוקבא בר חמא adds a second step to the משנה's polishing: thrusting the knife into the ground ten times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Thrusting the blade into the earth scrapes its whole surface. This method is called נעיצה.

keyTerms.meaning: He sticks or thrusts it in

phrases.english: Rav Ukva bar Ḥama said:
And he thrusts it ten times into the ground.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a requirement to the משנה's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The knife must also be thrust into the ground ten times.

steps.title: The ground must be hard, untilled earth
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע adds that the ground must be untilled, meaning hard earth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע said: And in ground that has not been worked.
steps.whatsHappening: Another אמורא narrows the rule: the earth must be untilled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Soft, plowed earth would not scrape the blade well. Hard ground rubs it clean.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said:
And in ground that is not tilled.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a detail to רב עוקבא בר חמא's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The thrusting must be done in hard, untilled earth.

steps.title: Only a smooth knife without notches
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא says this method works only for a good knife with no notches.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: And with a good knife that has no notches.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא limits the method to a smooth, undamaged knife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Forbidden food can stay stuck inside notches, where the earth cannot reach. Only a smooth blade gets fully scraped.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
And with a good knife that has no notches.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another condition to the rule of thrusting.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Thrusting works only for a smooth knife without notches.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports these rules
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches the same thing: a good knife without notches is thrust into the ground ten times.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught in a ברייתא: a good knife with no notches, one thrusts it ten times into the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up what רב עוקבא בר חמא and רב כהנא said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא mentions both the ten thrusts and the no-notches condition together. So these are not just the אמוראים' own ideas. They come from an earlier source.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (a ברייתא supports it)

phrases.english: It was also taught so:
A good knife that has no notches,
one thrusts it ten times into the ground.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the rulings of רב עוקבא בר חמא and רב כהנא.
steps.raayaObject: Thrusting a smooth knife ten times into the ground
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with the same wording

steps.title: This method is only for cold food
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע limits the thrusting method: it only allows using the knife for cold food.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע said: To eat cold food with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets a limit: thrusting is enough only for cutting cold food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Thrusting removes what is on the surface of the blade. It does not draw out absorbed taste, and hot food could pull that taste out. So for hot use a stronger koshering would be needed.
steps.whatToRemember: A smooth knife, thrust ten times into hard ground, may be used for cold food.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think נעיצה makes the knife fully kosher for every use. It covers cold food only.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said:
To eat cold food with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: לֶאֱכוֹל בָּהּ צוֹנֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the scope of the thrusting method.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Thrusting the knife is enough only for cutting cold food.

steps.title: שבור מלכא cleans the knife before cutting for מר יהודה
steps.stepSummary: A story: שבור מלכא cut an אתרוג, ate, and gave a slice to באטי בר טובי. Then he stuck the knife into the ground ten times before cutting a slice for מר יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like the story of מר יהודה and באטי בר טובי, who were sitting before King שבור. An אתרוג was brought before them. The king cut and ate, cut and gave to באטי בר טובי, then stuck the knife into the ground ten times, cut, and gave to מר יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story showing the cold-food rule in action. An אתרוג is cold food, and the king used נעיצה before serving the Jewish sage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a Persian king knew that thrusting a knife into the ground ten times made it fit for a careful Jew to eat cold food cut with it. This matches רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's ruling.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָא דְּמָר יְהוּדָה וּבָאטִי בַּר טוֹבִי
phrases.english: Like this story of Mar Yehuda and Bati bar Tuvi,
who were sitting before King Shapur.
They brought an etrog before them.
He cut and ate,

phrases.aramaic: פְּסַק וְהַב לֵיהּ לְבָאטִי בַּר טוֹבִי,
phrases.english: cut and gave to Bati bar Tuvi,
then stuck it ten times in the ground,
cut and gave to Mar Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּמָר יְהוּדָה וּבָאטִי בַּר טוֹבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the rule of thrusting the knife for cold food.
steps.raayaObject: Thrusting a knife ten times into the ground is used for cutting cold food
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of שבור מלכא with מר יהודה and באטי בר טובי

steps.title: באטי בר טובי asks why he was treated differently
steps.stepSummary: באטי בר טובי complains to the king: 'Am I not Jewish too?'
steps.simpleTranslation: באטי בר טובי said to him: And is that man not a Jew?
steps.whatsHappening: באטי בר טובי protests that the king did not clean the knife before cutting for him. This sets up the king's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He feels insulted. If the knife needed cleaning for מר יהודה, it should have needed cleaning for him as well.

keyTerms.meaning: That man (a polite way to refer to oneself)

phrases.english: Bati bar Tuvi said to him:

phrases.aramaic: וְהָהוּא גַּבְרָא לָאו בַּר יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא?
phrases.english: And is that man not a Jew?
phrases.notes: 'That man' is his polite way of talking about himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to the king's different treatment in the story.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the king cleaned the knife for מר יהודה but not for him

steps.title: The king: I trust that one is careful, not you
steps.stepSummary: שבור מלכא answers that he is sure מר יהודה is careful about הלכה, but not sure about באטי בר טובי.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: About that master I am certain, and about that master I am not certain.
steps.whatsHappening: The king explains his different treatment: he knew מר יהודה keeps the rules carefully.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The king made the effort only for someone he knew would care about it. He doubted that באטי בר טובי was that careful.

keyTerms.meaning: I am certain, I know for sure

phrases.english: He said to him:
About that master I am certain,
and about that master I am not certain.
phrases.notes: This second 'master' is באטי בר טובי himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מָר קִים לִי בְּגַוֵּיהּ
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The king knew מר יהודה is careful about הלכה but was unsure about באטי בר טובי.

steps.title: Another version: 'Remember what you did last night'
steps.stepSummary: Another version of the king's answer: he told באטי בר טובי to remember what he had done the night before.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say he said to him: Remember what you did last night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the king's reply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version the king points to something improper באטי בר טובי did the night before. That behavior showed he was not careful about הלכה, so there was no reason to clean the knife for him.
steps.whatToRemember: Either way, the king cleaned the knife only for the Jew he knew was careful. The story confirms that נעיצה works for cold food.

phrases.english: Some say he said to him:
Remember what you did last night.
phrases.notes: The king is hinting at something improper באטי did the night before, which showed he wasn't careful about הלכה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative version of the king's answer in step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: באטי בר טובי's own conduct the night before showed he was not careful about הלכה.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing השוכר את הפועל and finishing מסכת עבודה זרה
steps.stepSummary: The traditional הדרן formula closes the פרק השוכר את הפועל and announces that מסכת עבודה זרה is finished.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter 'One who hires a worker,' and with this, tractate עבודה זרה is complete.
steps.whatsHappening: This is not a new argument. It is the closing line that ends the פרק השוכר את הפועל and the whole מסכת עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words הדרן עלך are a promise to come back and learn this פרק again. The second half adds that this was the last פרק, so the entire מסכת is now finished. No question or proof is involved; it simply marks the end.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you: the traditional goodbye to a פרק when you finish it
One who hires a worker: the name of this פרק, taken from its opening words

steps.whatToRemember: With this line, the last פרק, השוכר את הפועל, is closed and all of מסכת עבודה זרה is complete. The last topic before it was keeping a knife clean of non-kosher food, ending with the story of שבור מלכא and the אתרוג.
steps.whyThisMatters: Saying הדרן at the end of a פרק or מסכת expresses that learning is never really finished: we plan to come back to it. Finishing a whole מסכת is traditionally celebrated with a סיום.

phrases.english: We will return to you, chapter 'One who hires a worker,'
and the tractate of עבודה זרה is finished.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: None: this is a standard closing formula
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comes after the last story (steps 9–12) about שבור מלכא, the knife and the אתרוג, and closes the פרק and the מסכת.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פרק השוכר את הפועל is complete, and with it the entire מסכת עבודה זרה is finished, with the hope of returning to learn it again.
